long_biography.plain_text:
Warren J. Wilson entered business by selling funnel cakes made from his grandmother's recipe at the Allentown Fair in 1969, using the proceeds to help pay for college. He later opened a mall shop, where he met Sara. Their shared interest in product development became a long-running entrepreneurial partnership.

The Wilsons expanded funnel cakes into theme parks, then created New York Style Bagel Chips and built their own factories when established manufacturers declined the unusual two-stage process. After selling that business to Nabisco, they developed Pretzel Crisps through Snack Factory, pairing food invention with nationwide retail distribution. The brand became a leading premium snack before Snack Factory was acquired by Snyder's-Lance in 2012.
